resources.string: Add themed shortcut to home screen
Shortcut request sent to your launcher.

Android has no way for an app to replace another app\'s icon across your whole phone. The launcher decides what it draws. DarkFrame therefore does not claim to restyle your home screen silently — it supports every mechanism Android actually provides, and tells you which one applies to your launcher.
Your launcher reads icon packs. Select DarkFrame in its settings and it will substitute icons itself. DarkFrame cannot make that selection for you — no launcher exposes an API for it.

Your launcher does not read icon packs, so DarkFrame can add a themed shortcut to your home screen for each app. The shortcut opens the app normally. It sits alongside the original entry rather than replacing it, your app drawer is unchanged, and some launchers add their own shadow or badge to pinned shortcuts.
Your launcher lets you change one app\'s icon at a time. Export the DarkFrame icon, then pick it in your launcher\'s own edit flow.
DarkFrame has not verified icon theming on your launcher. You can export any themed icon as a PNG and apply it however your launcher or theme engine allows.
Whatever your launcher supports, you can always export a themed icon as a PNG from its entry in the app list, and use it wherever you need it.

DarkFrame asks Android only for apps that have a launcher icon, which is the narrowest question that answers what it needs. It does not request broad package access. Apps without a launcher icon, and work-profile or Secure Folder apps, are not visible to DarkFrame — only your active home launcher may list those.
Pick a collection. Every one works with both DarkFrame artwork and icons generated from your installed apps.
These are the apps DarkFrame has handmade artwork for. Every other app on your device is themed too, from its own icon.
